book_context: Episodes are framed as successive failed 'educations': diplomacy and London, Darwinism, the press, Grant's Washington, teaching, and then, after a twenty-year silence, a new search for force and unity. Recurring mechanisms run through the selected chapters. 'A friend in power is a friend lost' recurs as a law. Pteraspis and Terebratula stand for fixed, unevolving types, and the begonia for showy uselessness. Older steamers serve as measures of acceleration. Chaos versus order and 'one sees what one brings' set up the later dynamic theory. Chapters 019–020 (Grant, the Gold Conspiracy, the 1869–70 'Session' article) are omitted, so Chapter 021 must carry minimal context for them. Chapters 024–025 are also omitted. Adams's wife's death, which falls between 022 and 023, is never narrated by the author. The abridgment must keep that silence and not explain the Rock Creek figure.
continuity_checks: Do not mention Adams's wife or her death.

Brice's quip concerns Cleveland, with the same remark applied to Harrison.
The Lamar formula is attributed to Lamar.
Hay and Adams had finished Lincoln and Jefferson/Madison respectively.

essential: Opening insistence that this is a story of education, meant to help the young. Education should train minds to react 'with vigor and economy', and society conspires to waste mind.

Twenty-year summary: no complaints against anyone; much work done in the dark; his generation's artists; King, Hay and Adams filling social gaps; tiredness and quitting the race. Narrate no events of the gap beyond what the author gives.
London hospital, January 1892, near his fifty-fourth birthday; return from the South Seas with La Farge; reluctance for new education.
Fantastic new Paris; La Farge asks about something simple in art and Adams shakes his head.
Return to Washington as to a stable; brief background on 1877, Evarts, Hay, and the Richardson houses on La Fayette Square; parents dead; a week at Thornes with Milnes Gaskell.
The Teutonic as a marvel against a stationary Europe, and the Niagara ratio.
Kipling aboard and the American/English gap in the blood, with King's wave-length joke.
Washington society detached from government; the 1892 election, with Brice's Cleveland quip and Adams's slight preference for Cleveland as an eighteenth-century remnant against 'King Banker'.
Why none of the trio holds office: no President ever invited him; Lamar's courteous formula; the friend promoted to power 'always lost'; Hay used but never given office, and laughing at himself.
Profit and loss of the twenty years: Hay's 'old Boutwell gambolling'; consideration versus ten thousand a year; three readers; King's high-stakes course still in doubt.
Americans lost the sense of worship and ideals, waste money, and are ignorant of the past.

St. Gaudens's figure at Rock Creek. Its meaning is assumed to be the oldest commonplace; observers see only what they bring. Leave the figure's occasion unexplained. Then railways and coal approaching British output, the bicycle, and the closing distrust of bankers.

title: TWENTY YEARS AFTER (1892)

verbatim.text: What one knows is, in youth, of little moment; they know enough who know how to learn.

verbatim.purpose: Marks the twenty-year gap without narrating it.
verbatim.text: Education had ended in 1871; life was complete in 1890; the rest mattered so little!
He went home as a horse goes back to his stable, because he knew nowhere else to go.

verbatim.purpose: First acceleration calculation, which anticipates the later law.
verbatim.text: As the Niagara was to the Teutonic--as 1860 was to 1890--so the Teutonic and 1890 must be to the next term--and then?
as though playing a garden hose on a thirsty and faded begonia.

verbatim.text: Like the others, the priest saw only what he brought. Like all great artists, St. Gaudens held up the mirror and no more.
At past fifty, Adams solemnly and painfully learned to ride the bicycle.

verbatim.purpose: Closing irony that sets up distrust of bankers.
verbatim.text: Even dead men allow themselves a few narrow prejudices.

voice_profile: Third-person autobiography in which the elderly Adams ironizes his younger self ('the young man', 'the private secretary', 'one'). He uses aphoristic, paradoxical sentences, often in triads or semicolon chains. Images are drawn from science, natural history and the market: earthworm, deep-sea fish, anvil, begonia, Pteraspis. The governing frame is 'education' and its constant failure. He pairs self-deprecation with sweeping historical generalization, hedges claims with 'perhaps' and 'as Adams felt it', and lands chapter-closing ironies as dry punchlines. Double hyphens mark interpolations and appositive cascades.
